title: Onboarding access latency map & cross-pod handbook
content:
Purpose
---
This working doc creates a practical, operational "access latency map" for new hires and contractors and pairs that with a cross-pod (engineering, product, infra, security) handbook for what to do when provisioning slips. Goal: reduce first-48h friction and reduce shadow-handovers. Treat as lightweight — iterate with SRE and infra-owner inputs.

Context / why we need this
---
Observed problems in last 6 months: slow repo and cloud access (avg 36h), inconsistent Slack invites for contractors, noisy manual escalations to managers on day 2. This causes lost momentum in the crucial first week and increases manager load.

High-level SLA targets (proposal)
---
- Day0 (within 4 hours): corporate email, badge/physical access request submitted (if on-site), calendar stub + HR welcome message
- Day0 (within 8 hours): Slack invite, Okta user created, basic SSO to docs (Confluence read), payroll form completed
- Day1 (within 24 hours): GitHub org invite, repo-level read access for primary team, ticketing tool (Linear/JIRA) viewer access
- Day2 (within 48 hours): dev cloud console role (limited), build/test infra access, staging project credentials, VPN/VPC routing where needed
- Day5 (within 5 business days): full prod access (per role), privileged secrets via vault, 2FA validated

Note: targets are intentionally graded — Day1 vs Day2 depend on vendor approvals and security review. We want measurable latency buckets.

Access Latency Map (practical checklist)
---
For each new hire, run this checklist and log timestamps in the onboarding tracker (sheet link in linked_artifacts). Leave a short timestamp note if something blocks.

Pre-onboard (HR / People Ops)
- Send offer + welcome packet (Day -7 to -1) — includes clear ask for personal email used for SSO, preferred name, time zone, and hardware preferences.
- Create Okta stub account w/ placeholder email (Day -1).
- Open onboarding ticket in JIRA: OPS-ONBOARD-<candidate initials> (assign to infra-runbook).

Day0 (first 8 hours) — People Ops + Manager + IT
- Confirm corporate email created and validated (timestamp).
- Slack invite sent (include intro snippets + manager + buddy).
- Add to team calendar + recurring 1:1 with manager.
- Hardware request kick (if requested) and a local contact for pickup.
- Onboard buddy assigned and introduced in Slack.

Day1 — Manager + Engineering lead + SRE
- GitHub org invite issued (link + role). If using GH Teams, add to team.
- Repo access: at minimum, read access to codebase & infra repo. If missing, escalate to "repo-access" on-call.
- Add to Linear/JIRA project; create a low-friction starter ticket (e.g., "Intro: run local dev setup").
- Add to internal docs group, Confluence team space, and shared drive folders.

Day2 — Infra & Security
- Provision development cloud account: ensure IAM roles follow least privilege patterns.
- Check that secrets manager access is denied until gating checklist passes.
- If on-prem or private deployment access required, schedule SRE window.

Day3–5 — Product & QA
- Grant staging/QA project access; add to test-runner groups.
- Schedule an onboarding pairing session with product or QA.

Escalation flow (when latency > target)
---
1) Owner (People Ops) pings infra-runbook (Slack) and files/update JIRA OPS-ONBOARD ticket.
2) If no response in 4 business hours: pager-style escalate to on-call infra (rota list).
3) If still unresolved at 24 hours: notify manager + ERT (people-ops lead + eng manager). Include timestamps and the last action taken.

Interview rubric (light version for fast hires)
---
This section is intentionally compact — use for hiring sprints where speed matters. Full rubric lives in Confluence link above.

Core sections (each scored 1–4, 4 = strong)
- Problem solving (clarity of thought, structured approach, tradeoff analysis)
- System design (for infra/platform roles) OR Product sense (for PM/PD roles)
- Technical proficiency (languages/tools relevant to role)
- Ownership & communication (evidence of owning projects, cross-team collaboration)
- Culture fit / values alignment (bias for impact, operational humility)

Quick calibration notes for interviewers:
- Use concrete past work examples. Ask for measurable outcomes (latency improvements, cost savings, uptime).
- For ambiguous answers, push for tradeoffs and constraints definitions.

Hiring plan mini-template (for hiring manager to fill quickly)
---
- Role summary: one-sentence impact statement.
- Must-have signals (3): e.g., experience with infra-as-code, monitoring, cost ops.
- Nice-to-have signals (2–3): e.g., public infra contributions, prior PLG experience.
- Interview loop draft (3–5 interviews): recruiter screen (30m), technical (45m), system design (60m), manager (45m), peer (30m).
- Expected ramp milestones (30/60/90 day outputs): e.g., "day30: run a small oncall shadow; day90: own first small rollout".
- Hiring urgency: low/medium/high and suggested sourcing channels.

Onboarding checklists & micro-rituals (manager + buddy)
---
Manager responsibilities (day0–7):
- Day0 welcome + priority list + 1:1 scheduled.
- Day1 pairing session: repo walkthrough and first-touch ticket.
- Provide 30/60/90 outcomes and clear acceptance criteria.
- End of week1: 30-min checkpoint for blockers and access audit.

Buddy responsibilities (days 0–14):
- Quick-run of dev setup (share exact commands).
- Provide a list of 3 starter tickets with setup difficulty levels.
- Shadow pairing: 2x 60-min sessions in week1.

Operational templates (copyable snippets)
---
- Slack intro template: "Hey team — please welcome <name> (role) joining <team>. Primary buddy: <buddy>."
- Repo request template (send to infra): "Please grant read access to GH user <handle> for repos: <list>. Required by: <date>. JIRA OPS-ONBOARD-<id>"

Open questions & TODOs (for next iteration)
---
- Do we automate repo invites via GH apps? (Priya to follow up with infra team, ticket JIRA-OPS-4888).
- Measure current baseline latency per role — build dashboard (SRE + people-ops).
- Contractor onboarding deviations: add a short branch for vendor approvals and PO signer map.

Quick wins to reduce friction immediately
---
- Standardize one onboarding starter ticket per team in Linear (templated).
- Pre-approve common infra roles for IC1–IC3 to avoid manual gating.
- Create a single Slack channel for day0 escalations with an on-call rotation.

Appendix: sample timestamp log (copy into trackers)
---
- offer_sent: 2025-11-01T09:12Z
- okta_created: 2025-11-03T08:05Z

Notes to reviewers
---
This doc is an operational draft. Priorities for review: 1) Are SLA targets realistic for infra? 2) Does security team require different gating windows? 3) Missing stakeholders? Add comments inline or ping me in #people-ops.

----
